I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what I would do because it fits the climate and irrigation conditions on the North China Plain, I know the management well, and at 62 I would rather run a steady, familiar system than chase a riskier crop that needs more labor, more marketing, or more technical management. I would not split into many crops. I would keep the whole farm in one wheat-maize rotation, use improved seed, put fertilizer on in a moderate way, irrigate only at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to the times when disease, weeds, or insects are most likely to matter. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical, common, and easier for me to manage than deeper ploughing every season. Since you did not give a land size, I am assuming I am planning for 10 mu of land and using the full 10 mu in this rotation.
